control.name: Segregation of Duties Monitoring
control.risk: Failure to identify and resolve incompatible access combinations could allow a user to initiate and conceal an error or fraud without independent review, resulting in unauthorized or inaccurate financial transactions.
control.control_description: Management performs periodic analysis of complete active user entitlement populations against the approved segregation of duties matrix and remediates or formally mitigates identified conflicts.
control.objective: Incompatible duties within and across in scope systems are identified, prevented, remediated, or mitigated through approved compensating controls.
control.activity: Evaluate complete active user entitlement populations against the approved, versioned SoD rule matrix, including cross application combinations.
control.frequency: Weekly detective monitoring; formal management review at least quarterly
control.population: All active human, privileged, generic, and applicable service accounts with roles and permissions across in scope systems.

SOD-01.assertion: The applied rule set matches the current approved SoD matrix.

SOD-02.assertion: No active user holds an unmitigated incompatible access combination.

SOD-03.assertion: Cross application conflicts are included where the business process spans systems.

SOD-04.assertion: Accepted conflicts have a current owner, approval, compensating control, and periodic reassessment.

findings.assertion: No active user holds an unmitigated incompatible access combination.
findings.risk_statement: A user could create or alter a vendor and release payment to that vendor
findings.detail: Active incompatible access is not effectively mitigated: no approved exception.
findings.remediation: Remove or redesign one side of the conflicting access, or obtain formal approval for a time bound compensating control.
findings.mitigation: Review relevant transactions during the exposure period and validate that an independent control detected or prevented inappropriate activity.
findings.root_cause: Determine whether role design, provisioning bypass, matrix mapping, system integration, or periodic review failed.
findings.closure_evidence: Entitlement evidence from before and after the change, an approved exception if applicable, the transaction lookback, and control owner approval.
findings.escalation: Escalate immediately for conflicts capable of creating and approving or releasing financial transactions without independent review.

findings.detail: Accepted conflict governance is not current or effective: latest compensating control test result is failed.
findings.remediation: Remove conflicting access or renew and approve the exception with an owned, effective compensating control and reassessment date.
findings.mitigation: Perform the overdue or failed compensating control review and a transaction lookback for the unsupported period.
findings.root_cause: Determine why exception ownership, expiry monitoring, evidence collection, or control performance failed.
findings.closure_evidence: Current approval, owner, compensating control test, reassessment date, lookback conclusion, and control owner approval.
findings.escalation: Escalate immediately when a critical conflict has no effective compensating control; otherwise at the response SLA.
